messages:
alex: heads-up — started seeing a cluster of customer escalations after the rate-limit rollout at 09:00 UTC, mostly 429s + a couple of billing 402s. putting notes here for triage.
maria: which customers? any shared pattern (region, model, auth)?
alex: mostly two enterprise tenants (ACME Inc, BrightData). requests are short but bursty — lots of concurrent websocket streams hitting chat endpoint.
sam: can you paste a sample request/response? want to check headers and retry-after.
alex: here's a sample curl they sent: ``curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"status"}]}'`` Response: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests, body `{"error":"rate_limited"}` and no Retry-After header.
luke: no Retry-After is surprising — our rate middleware should add it. opsbot: ratepolicy-v2 deployed to 4 clusters at 09:00 UTC (canary=10%).
sophie: billing-bot logged 402s for ACME at ~09:12 UTC, message: "insufficient balance for reserved throughput". different root cause.
maria: so two signals: quota exhaustion (billing) and policy enforcement for burst control. do we know which customers were in canary?
alex: opsbot shows ACME in canary list for us-east-1. BrightData not in canary but they triggered fallback to ratepolicy-v2 due to smart routing.
sam: for reproducer, can we run a controlled burst from staging client to emulate websocket fanout? include same auth tokens? don't use prod tokens.
luke: oncall (sophie) — can you confirm whether the rate middleware sent X-RateLimit-* headers for the hits that 429'd? logs show middleware error writing headers for certain keepalive connections.
sophie: looking now — there's an Nginx upstream timeout that caused the second half of the headers not to flush. some proxies dropped Retry-After. opening a small fix to ensure middleware writes header earlier.
maria: while that's in flight, let's decide rollback criteria: if >5% of production traffic is 429ing for >10m or any SEV1 customer impacted -> rollback. agree?alEX: typo but agree 👍 (reaction :thumbsup:).
alex: also, for billing 402s, ops — confirm whether reserved throughput billing window alignment changed with the rate cut.
billing-bot: invoice-service: queued usage reconciliation job for ACME at 09:15 UTC; found negative balance after rate policy applied.
sam: temporary mitigation: increase token bucket burst for canary group by +20% and push policy patch that preserves Retry-After header write order. canary increase should be targeted and limited.
maria: who can push the patch and who will watch metrics? sam/luke?
luke: I'll push the header fix to canary only (cluster-3) now, sam will adjust bucket window. watching p50/p95 latency and 429 rate.
sophie: I'll coordinate support replies and send a short explainer to ACME & BrightData: "We rolled a targeted rate policy; we're reverting header behavior and adjusting bucket sizing while we validate".
alex: timeline: header fix live 09:32, bucket tweak live 09:38. canary 10% -> monitor 15m, if 429s drop <0.5% and no new 402s, continue staged rollout.
maria: if 429s don't improve in 15m or billing 402s persist -> initiate rollback of policy to previous version and open emergency postmortem.
sam: noted. I'll also add a temporary transparent header in the edge to surface which policy version served each request: `X-RW-Policy: v2-canary` to help customers correlate.
luke: pushed header fix to canary, visible in logs: `policy_write_ok`. sophie — draft is ready to send.
sophie: sending now. ACME reply: "Thanks, we can throttle client-side too for now." They asked for a window to sync tomorrow.
alex: closing loop — monitoring dashboards updated, alert threshold lowered for 429 spike. will follow up in #incidents if anything regresses.
maria: great coordination, thanks everyone.
(opsbot automated): deployment note: rollback plan registered (id: rp-2024-09-10-01) if triggered.
_meta: This thread simulates a short support-escalation and operational coordination chat about a rate-limit rollout where both policy enforcement and billing alignment caused customer impact. Messages are intentionally concise and include a reproducer snippet and action timeline.
